subject: social
title: Good Citizens
about: Rights versus responsibilities, ways people make their community better (recycling, volunteering, picking up litter) and how to settle disagreements kindly. NC 1.C&G.1.3, 1.C&G.1.4 and 1.B.1.4.
tip: When he says 'that's not fair', ask: is that a right or a responsibility, and what is a compromise?

cards.q: What do we call a member of a community or country?
cards.note: A citizen belongs to a community and helps take care of it.

cards.q: What do we call a freedom you are allowed to have?
cards.note: A right is something you are allowed to have, like being treated fairly.

cards.q: What do we call a job or duty you should do?
cards.note: A responsibility is something you should do, like cleaning up your toys.

cards.q: Is doing your homework a right or a responsibility?
cards.note: Homework is a job you should do. That makes it a responsibility.

cards.q: Is saying what you think a right or a responsibility?
cards.note: You are allowed to share your ideas. That makes it a right.

cards.q: Is following the rules a right or a responsibility?
cards.note: Following the rules is something you should do. That makes it a responsibility.

cards.q: Is being treated fairly a right or a responsibility?
cards.note: Everyone should be treated fairly. That is a right.

cards.q: Is taking care of your pet a right or a responsibility?
cards.note: A pet needs food, water and love. Caring for it is a responsibility.

cards.q: What do we call making old cans, paper and bottles into new things?
cards.note: Recycling means less trash and new things made from old ones.

cards.q: What do we call helping others without being paid?
cards.note: Volunteers help because they want to, not for money.

cards.q: What do we call a place where neighbors grow vegetables together?
cards.note: A community garden gives neighbors fresh food and a place to work together.

cards.q: You see litter at the park. What do you do?
cards.note: Pick it up and put it in the trash can. That keeps the park clean for everyone.

cards.q: What can you give to a food pantry to help hungry families?
cards.note: A food pantry gives food to families who need it.

cards.q: Two friends want the same ball. What can they do?
cards.note: Taking turns means both friends get to play.

cards.q: Each person gives up a little so everyone agrees. What is that called?
cards.note: In a compromise, nobody gets everything, but everyone gets something.

cards.q: What should you use to solve a problem with a friend?
cards.note: Kind words help friends fix a problem together.

cards.q: What do you do while a friend is talking?
cards.note: Listening shows your friend that you care about their idea.

cards.q: Classmates cannot agree. Who can help?
cards.note: A teacher can help everyone talk it out and find a fair way.

cards.q: What do we call working together nicely to finish a job?
cards.note: Cooperation means everyone does a part and the job gets done.

cards.q: You bumped a friend by accident. What do you say?
cards.note: Saying sorry helps a friend feel better.
